newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lightning strikes empty Air NZ plane.
newsitem.headline: Lightning strikes empty Air NZ plane.

text.p: An Air New Zealand plane was hit by lightning and the airline's Wellington Airport domestic terminal was flooded as a severe electrical and hail storm hit the region early on Monday, NZPA reported.
Air NZ duty manager Kevin Williams said the empty Boeing 767 was flying from Christchurch to Wellington to take on passengers for for a 7.15 a.m. flight to Sydney.
It was hit by two lightning strikes.
Williams said the flight was delayed while the plane was checked for damage.
Wellington Airport's domestic terminal was closed after a heavy hailstorm about 6 a.m. caused flooding.
Wellington Airport Company communications manager Heather Hayden said the hail built up on the terminal's roof and as it melted "streams of water" started to run through the roof.
"There are big puddles of water in the terminal itself," Hayden said.
The terminal was closed not only because of the flooding but also for safety so wiring could be checked.
Williams said passengers could not be checked in as water had got into the computer system.
Some flights had been rescheduled through the international terminal. Williams said three departing and three incoming flights had been cancelled by 8.15 a.m.
